title: Samut Prakan Food Guide 2026 — Seafood, Bang Bo Snakeskin Fish | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: What to eat in Samut Prakan, Thailand: beachside seafood at Bang Pu, Bang Bo snakeskin gourami, fresh cockles at Pak Nam Market, and old-market eats in Bang Phli — with real shops, real neighbourhoods, and rough prices.
keywords: Samut Prakan food, Bang Pu seafood, Bang Bo snakeskin fish, Pak Nam cockles, Samut Prakan souvenirs, Bang Phli old market
eyebrow: Where to eat in Samut Prakan
intro: Samut Prakan is a coastal province less than an hour's drive from Bangkok, so most of the food here revolves around the sea — beachside seafood at Bang Pu, fresh cockles straight off the boats at Pak Nam Market, the legendary Bang Bo snakeskin gourami that locals bring home as a gift, and the old-fashioned eats of the Bang Phli antique market. This is the food people from Pak Nam actually eat, and it's worth the trip.

blocks.html: When you think about food in Samut Prakan, the first word that comes to mind for a lot of people is Pak Nam — because this is the town where the Chao Phraya River meets the Gulf of Thailand, so seafood here is fresher and noticeably cheaper than in Bangkok. We've split the things worth trying into groups: beachside seafood at Bang Pu, cockles and other shellfish at Pak Nam Market, the Bang Bo snakeskin gourami that's the province's signature gift, and the snacky eats of the Bang Phli old market that you can graze on all day.

Bang Pu is one of the closest spots to Bangkok where you can eat seafood right by the sea. The draw is sitting in the sea breeze, watching the seagulls in winter (roughly November to February), and ordering fresh seafood to go with it. Most of the restaurants are around the Bang Pu Recreation Centre and Thetsaban Bang Pu Road. Prices depend on what you order, but on the whole you'll pay around 250–500 THB a head and walk away full.

items.name: Moken Bang Pu
items.blurb: A relaxed seaside spot where you can sit in the breeze and watch the seagulls in winter. The ingredients are fresh, the flavours are balanced, and it's a good place to settle in for a long evening. This is the name that comes up most often when people talk about Bang Pu.

items.name: Sai Lom Bang Pu
items.blurb: A seaside seafood restaurant a lot of people love for the evening atmosphere. Popular orders are baked seafood curry with cheese, oysters, tom yum goong, and cockle salad. Open daily, roughly 11:00–22:00.

items.name: Krua Boonlert Bang Pu
items.blurb: A roomy place with an air-conditioned section for lunch and an open-air section for the evening breeze. Standout dishes people mention are horseshoe-crab egg salad, blue-crab papaya salad, and garlic-fried soft-shell crab. It's an old-timer that's been going a long time.

items.name: Lung Waen Seafood
items.blurb: A laid-back Thai-seafood spot with outdoor seating and bold, punchy flavours that suit anyone who likes things spicy. The ingredients are fresh and it's a good place to come with a group.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: If you want to see the flocks of seagulls at Bang Pu, come between November and February when the birds are at their thickest. Go in the late afternoon and you can eat while watching the sun set over the sea.

blocks.text: Cockles and Shellfish at Pak Nam Market

blocks.html: Pak Nam Market is the old market in the centre of Samut Prakan town. The stalls a lot of people come for are the fresh cockles and seafood — because it's right by the river mouth, the catch is fresh and the prices beat Bangkok. Big cockles blanched until they're just barely cooked, dipped in spicy seafood sauce, are the thing you have to try when you come to this market.

items: Blanched cockles — the star of Pak Nam Market, blanched until just barely cooked so the meat stays juicy, dipped in punchy seafood sauce. You can buy them fresh to blanch yourself or already blanched and ready to eat.
Mussels and surf clams — the other shellfish sold alongside them; stir-fry them in chilli sauce or roasted chilli paste, or just blanch and dip.
Fresh prawns, crab, and fish — the fish stalls at Pak Nam have plenty to choose from depending on the season, prices are negotiable, and they're good to take home and cook yourself.
Stalls people talk about — several cockle stalls at Pak Nam Market have regulars, like Je Ang, Hoy Khrang Baan, and Hiw Hoy. Walk around and pick whichever has the freshest-looking catch.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Cockles are something to be careful with when it comes to cleanliness and freshness. If you eat them barely cooked, pick a stall that sells fast and turns its stock over quickly and where the catch looks fresh. If you have a sensitive stomach, ordering them fully cooked is the safer bet.

blocks.text: Bang Bo Snakeskin Gourami, the Provincial Souvenir

blocks.html: If you're going to buy one souvenir from Samut Prakan, Bang Bo snakeskin gourami (pla salid) is locals' first answer. Bang Bo district raises the fish in brackish ponds where red water-fleas are the natural food, which gives the flesh a firm, rich texture. That's why, whenever good snakeskin gourami comes up, Bang Bo is one of the first names people think of.

items.name: Mae Amnuay Bang Bo Snakeskin Fish
items.blurb: A long-running snakeskin-fish shop on the Old Sukhumvit Road that's been part of Bang Bo for decades. They use a traditional curing recipe, with both the fragrant soft-fleshed style and the firmer ice-cured style — pick according to your budget.

items.name: Sun-Dried Fish, Fried Hot
items.blurb: If you want to eat right at the shop, plenty of vendors fry up fresh sun-dried snakeskin fish to go with hot rice and sour mango — a simple meal that's seriously good.

blocks.title: How to pick
blocks.html: Bang Bo snakeskin gourami comes in two main styles. The fragrant kind is cured longer, so the flesh is softer and more aromatic, and it costs more. The ice-cured kind is cheaper and firmer. If you're buying it as a gift for elders, the fragrant kind looks like the more thoughtful choice.

blocks.text: Eats at the Bang Phli Old Market

blocks.html: The Bang Phli antique market is a canalside market more than a hundred years old, sitting right next to Wat Bang Phli Yai Nai (Luang Pho To). You can stroll and graze on both savoury and sweet things amid old wooden houses. Most stalls are open from morning to early afternoon, so it's best for an early weekend walk.

items: Thick-broth kuay jab — the kuay jab (rolled rice-noodle soup) stalls at Bang Phli market are a favourite, with a thick, rich broth and tender offal.
Kuay tiew pak mo — thin, soft steamed rice rolls with a generous filling, the kind of snack you find in an old market like this.
Thai and old-fashioned sweets — layered khanom chan, grilled sticky rice, red sticky rice, and old-style coconut-milk ice cream to graze on as you walk.
Processed seafood and souvenirs — both snacks and gifts to carry home, at market prices that aren't expensive.

blocks.html: Beyond Bang Phli, the town district of Mueang has more old markets to walk and eat through, like the Pak Nam Market area, which besides seafood also has snacks, noodles, and old-style coffee shops scattered around. You can carry on from buying your cockles.

If you have the time and really want fresh seafood at good prices, drive past Bang Bo towards Khlong Dan (in Bang Bo district). It's a seafood spot where prices are gentler than on the town side, and most of the restaurants are local places that get their catch from the area's fishing boats.

items.name: Dan Rim Le Café Khlong Dan
items.blurb: A seafront seafood spot with a good view, reasonable prices, and solid flavours — a nice place to settle in for the evening breeze.

items.name: Pom-T Seafood Khlong Dan
items.blurb: A well-known spot in the Khlong Dan area with fresh seafood at friendly prices. Popular orders include hoy jor (crab rolls) and fried sea bass with fish sauce.

items.name: Kor Tae Seafood
items.blurb: A local seafood place that people around Khlong Dan recommend. The catch is fresh, prices are low, and the focus is squarely on the freshness of the ingredients.

blocks.text: A Half-Day Food Trip in Samut Prakan

items.activity: Walk Pak Nam Market and buy cockles and seafood
items.note: Pick a stall with fresh-looking, fast-moving stock

items.activity: Stop for noodles or old-style coffee in the Pak Nam old-market area
items.note: Plenty of snack vendors to choose from

items.activity: Drive to Bang Pu and eat seafood by the sea
items.note: In winter you'll get to watch the seagulls too

items.activity: Sit in the breeze and watch the sunset on the Bang Pu seafront
items.note: An easy way to close out the trip

items.activity: Walk the Bang Phli antique market and try kuay jab and Thai sweets
items.note: Open morning to early afternoon — go early for the full spread

items.activity: Pay respects to Luang Pho To at Wat Bang Phli Yai Nai
items.note: Right next to the market, easy to carry on to

items.activity: Stop at a Bang Bo snakeskin-fish shop and buy souvenirs to take home
items.note: Go for the fragrant kind if it's a gift for elders

faq.q: What food should you try in Samut Prakan?
faq.a: Top of the list is beachside seafood at Bang Pu, fresh cockles from Pak Nam Market, and Bang Bo snakeskin gourami, the province's signature souvenir. If you like browsing old markets, the Bang Phli antique market has plenty of snacks and Thai sweets to taste.

faq.q: Which seafood restaurant is good at Bang Pu?
faq.a: The names people recommend most are Moken, Sai Lom Bang Pu, and Krua Boonlert. Most are around Thetsaban Bang Pu Road and the seafront, at roughly 250–500 THB a head. Come in the late afternoon so you can stay for the sunset.

faq.q: Where do you buy Bang Bo snakeskin fish, and how do you choose?
faq.a: The well-known shop is Mae Amnuay on the Old Sukhumvit Road. There are two styles to choose from: the fragrant soft-fleshed kind, which costs more, and the firmer ice-cured kind, which is cheaper. If you're buying it as a gift for elders, the fragrant kind looks like the more thoughtful choice.

faq.q: Can you eat the cockles at Pak Nam Market raw?
faq.a: Most people blanch them until just barely cooked so the meat stays juicy, but cockles are something to be careful with on freshness. If you have a sensitive stomach, order them fully cooked to be safe, and pick a stall that sells well and turns its stock over quickly.

faq.q: Is Samut Prakan good for a day trip focused on food?
faq.a: Very much so, since it's less than an hour's drive from Bangkok. Walk the Bang Phli or Pak Nam market in the morning, buy Bang Bo snakeskin fish at midday, and eat seafood by the sea at Bang Pu in the afternoon — an easy half- to full-day trip.
